retro:
# Team 5 retrospective, PR #12831

## What worked
- Author gate and bounded read-only security triage preceded reviewer lifecycle and all PR execution (none was needed).
- Fresh native Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh identities were verified through startup receipts plus actual transcript model/effort metadata. Legacy role keys were not treated as model evidence.
- Both independent finals existed before either report was read. Post-final adjudication was separately labelled, with unchanged finals and equal questions.
- Source-only scope resolved the material error-propagation question without generic test filler or risky live firewall experiments. Raw API envelopes, stderr and statuses were retained.
- The conditional upgrade hypothesis was narrowed rather than inflated into a verified defect; an unsupported exact retry count was explicitly withdrawn privately before publication.

## Deviations and preserved history
1. Coordinator pretty-printed the complete owned-pane layout metadata (own-layout-01.stdout), exceeding the requested 60-line aggregate output bound. A character slice was unnecessary but did not actually truncate this output. No policy/source or technical evidence was in that output. Later metadata outputs select required fields.
2. Initial coordinator policy reads requested 60 content lines. Tool continuation metadata may bring the whole response over 60 lines. The subsequently appended workflow correction now reserves overhead using at most 50 content lines. The coordinator read every required tail fully and switched to 50-line reads on discovering that update. This is not retroactive compliance. Opus similarly reported initial 55-line reads before encountering the new reservation. Native history remains unchanged.
3. Opus used a width-limited locator once, then read all relied-on ranges fully. The truncated locator is not treated as complete evidence.
4. The first three Opus fetches did not individually preassert their HTTP-status receipt targets, although those targets remained within its asserted evidence directory. Later fetches individually guarded all four destinations. Successful saved transport/status and source bytes remain usable for source claims; no claim of complete per-target process compliance is made.
5. Read-only setup errors were retained: coordinator initially guessed nonexistent role-specific prompt filenames, and the assertion failed before any reviewer dispatch; it then enumerated filenames and dispatched the verified reviewer.md path. Opus had wrong-filename/JSON-shape locator errors; Sol reported a tree-read and tree-filter error. None supplied a technical conclusion.

No runtime isolation failure occurred because no runtime experiment, test or probe ran. No host mutation, pattern killing, account lookup, mountinfo/global process discovery, public posting or intentional persistent-memory writes were performed. Native automatic history is preserved. No reviewed source or raw failed evidence was deleted.

## Evidence retained for public claims
Only complete pinned migration/driver/installer source, the fully inspected test as source, upstream UFW normal-return/error behavior, and explicit control-flow reasoning. No broad test totals, four-rerun claim, package equivalence, full upgrade claim or historical runtime result is carried forward as current validation. Process deviations do not leave these narrow source facts or independent assessments unresolved.

## Improvements
State the 50-content-line allowance in the very first dispatch to reserve tool overhead, while maintaining the overall 60-line bound. Generate metadata summaries without pretty-printing full structures. Require each fetch receipt destination in the literal target inventory. Continue distinguishing plausible backend interactions from a verified end-to-end upgrade conclusion. No confirmed Omadev/toolkit bug or desktop-resource issue was found; neither was used. Technical conclusions stay assignment-local.
comment:
**Verified by source inspection:** At `a49077e7`, the status/deletion error-handling finding in the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12831#issuecomment-5775644743) is resolved. The migration now checks UFW command status separately from deletion output, and exits nonzero on failure.

| Condition | Current source path |
|---|---|
| UFW is absent | Existing successful no-op is preserved |
| Status query, deletion, or scoped-rule addition fails | Migration exits nonzero; the driver stops before writing its completion marker |
| Deletion succeeds or finds no matching rule | Processing continues to the scoped rules |

The marker ordering in `bin/omarchy-migrate:89-96` therefore leaves the reported failed work pending for retry. The earlier successful-path repair remains in place: delete the legacy unrestricted UDP/TCP specifications, then add the six RFC1918-scoped rules. This does not change the distinction between private source addresses and trusted Wi-Fi networks.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source comparison of the previous/current migration, migration-driver control flow, installer, new test, and upstream UFW 0.36.2 behavior. No tests were executed in this follow-up; earlier runtime results were not repeated. Live filtering, rule persistence on this revision, LocalSend transfers, and full upgrade behavior remain untested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Fresh independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, followed by Astra Medium coordination and source-evidence adjudication.
